pages.name: Three bars, one rectangle
pages.text: A bracket keeps `x + 5` together as one bar, an `x`-bar with 5 squares on its end. Stack three and you have `3(x + 5)`, a rectangle that splits into `3x` and 15. At `x = 4` both make 27, and sliding `x` keeps them equal.

pages.name: Four bars
pages.task: The number outside, the [[factor]], multiplies each term inside. [[Expand]] `4(x + 5)`: write it without the bracket.
pages.why: Each of the 4 rows is `x + 5`, so the rectangle holds 4 `x`-bars, `4x`, and 4 rows of 5 squares, 20. So `4(x + 5) = 4x + 20`, and at `x = 2` both make 28.

pages.name: Keep the 5
pages.text: An easy slip is to multiply the `x` and forget the 5, writing `3x + 5`. The rectangle's right part holds 15 squares, not 5. At `x = 2`, `3(x + 5)` and `3x + 15` make 21, but `3x + 5` makes 11.

pages.task: Each row is two `x`-bars with 4 cut off. Expand `3(2x − 4)`.
pages.why: The rectangle holds 6 `x`-bars, `6x`, and each of the 3 rows has 4 cut off, `3 × 4 = 12` in all. So `3(2x − 4) = 6x − 12`, and at `x = 5` both make 18.

pages.name: A letter outside
pages.text: `R = R₀(1 + αΔT)` gives the resistance `R` after a temperature change `ΔT`, where `R₀` is the original resistance. Expanded, `R = R₀ + R₀αΔT`: the original `R₀` plus a thin strip, the extra resistance when a metal warms. For an example winding of 2.0 Ω cold and 2.4 Ω after a run, the strip is `2.4 − 2.0 = 0.4` Ω.

pages.name: A minus in front
pages.text: A minus in front takes away the whole bracket, which multiplies each term inside by `−1`, so every sign inside changes: `−(6x − 5) = −6x + 5`. A rectangle cannot show that, so try a number. At `x = 2` both make `−7`, but the slip `−6x − 5` makes `−17`.

pages.name: Two brackets
pages.why: `4(x + 3) = 4x + 12` and `2(x − 1) = 2x − 2`. Then `4x + 2x = 6x` and `12 − 2 = 10`, so the answer is `6x + 10`. At `x = 1` both make 16.

pages.name: Minus before a bracket
pages.why: The minus in front changes both signs inside, so `8x − (6x − 5) = 8x − 6x + 5`, which is `2x + 5`. At `x = 3` both make 11.

pages.alt: Try x equals 3. 8x minus (6x minus 5) makes 24 minus 13 equals 11. 2x plus 5 makes 6 plus 5 equals 11.
